name: Stepantsminda Village Center
description: The main hub where the marshrutkas stop and most guesthouses, small shops, and simple restaurants cluster. It is walkable end to end and offers the best odds of finding a room, a meal, and a working SIM signal. Views of Mount Kazbek loom over the square.
vibe: Rustic, functional, quietly busy in summer
bestFor: First-time visitors and anyone wanting easy access to transport and food
pros: Central for transport to and from Tbilisi
cons: Can feel busy and touristy in high season

name: Gergeti Village
tagline: Across the river, below the church
description: A quieter cluster of homes and guesthouses on the far bank of the Terek, right beneath the trail up to the Gergeti Trinity Church. It feels calmer and more residential than the center, with superb church-and-Kazbek views and an easy start point for the walk uphill.
bestFor: Slow travelers who want calm and quick trail access
pros: Closest base to the Gergeti Trinity Church trail
cons: Slightly removed from shops and transport

name: Sameba Ridge Area
description: The high ground around the Gergeti Trinity Church (Tsminda Sameba), reached by 4x4 taxi or a steep walk. There is little accommodation right at the ridge, but the boutique hotels on the upper slopes trade proximity to services for panoramic, elevated views straight at Mount Kazbek.
bestFor: Photographers and those seeking the biggest views
cons: Needs a 4x4 or a steep climb

name: Juta Valley
tagline: A trekking base beyond the village
description: A small, remote highland settlement roughly an hour away by rough road, prized as a launch point for the Chaukhi massif and the Juta to Roshka trek. Accommodation is limited to seasonal guesthouses and eco-camps, and it is far quieter and wilder than Stepantsminda itself.
bestFor: Trekkers wanting deep nature and solitude
cons: Very basic services and seasonal only
Rough access road, best with a 4x4
